original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Can scripts/shared_point_circuit.py:SharedPointCircuit.__init__ emit the same merge/lookup DAG (same args/core/union/provenance/outputs/active/merged_additions and the same circuit_sha256) with a tighter construction loop, so full-size shared-point builds stay fieldwise identical?
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one measured replay bottleneck with before/after wall time and retained checks. Expertise override selected verifier-engineering after open tooling PR #2039 left SharedPointCircuit.__init__ merge/lookup construction as an explicit next question (stated on the partial-swap fork; this package applies the same construction object on the canonical shared_point_circuit.py producer, which still had the historical loop). Profiling named the per-common-point merge loop (repeated sorted(active), per-node generator unpacks, repeated attribute lookups) as the construction bottleneck; verify digests are a different object already claimed by #1994/#2039.
bottleneck_link: Side result on review throughput: shared-point and bit-compression certificates construct SharedPointCircuit(46) before verify. A faster identical constructor does not change kappa or the binding complex supplier.
stop_rule: Ship an equivalence-preserving SharedPointCircuit.__init__ change with frozen baseline, identical structure and receipts on the historical h=46 circuit, registered replay and a measured before/after median. Do not reopen verify digests, ExclusionCircuit/DisjointTensor support masks (#2001), or run the selected cold frontier replay.
evidence: PASS_SHARED_POINT_INIT via research/shared-point-init/verify.py (also under -O); PASS_IDENTICAL_SHARED_POINT_INIT_RECEIPTS via benchmark.py; bit-compression certificate does not pin scripts/shared_point_circuit.py in source_sha256.
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for orientation, overlap search, profiling, implementation, packaging, benchmarking and writing. Not independent human peer review.

open_questions.question: Should research/bit-compression-provenance refresh its live scripts/shared_point_circuit.py SHA-256 pin after this equivalence-preserving constructor rewrite?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That provenance package binds working-tree bytes of shared_point_circuit.py; leaving the old pin keeps this tooling PR focused, but a later full provenance replay on main would see a hash mismatch until refreshed.
open_questions.first_step: Open a dedicated provenance follow-up that only rewrites the shared_point_circuit.py entry in SOURCES.json after confirming circuit_sha256 identity.
open_questions.blocked_by: Pin repair is outside this tooling change.

open_questions.question: Is the same merge/lookup construction rewrite worth applying to scripts/partial_swap/shared.py:SharedPointCircuit.__init__ (the fork named in #2039's open question)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The partial-swap producer copy still uses the historical loop; large skip-strip builds spend substantial wall time constructing that DAG.
open_questions.first_step: After #2039's verify-digest change lands or in a follow-up that updates the three partial_swap source_sha256 certificate pins, port this constructor rewrite and remeasure.
open_questions.blocked_by: Open #2039 already edits that file's verify path and its certificate pin; this package stays on the canonical producer to avoid a pin conflict.
